candidate.blueprint_locator: Reduction of Risk Potential, Related Activity Statements and System-Specific Assessments: perform focused assessments; recognize trends and changes in client condition and intervene as needed; perform system-specific assessments
candidate.blueprint_topic: Reduction of Risk Potential — cardiovascular focused assessment / new murmur follow-up
candidate.educational_objective: Recognize a newly identified murmur as an abnormal cardiovascular assessment finding that should be documented and reported for further evaluation.

options.A: Document the new finding and notify the health care provider
options.B: Assume the murmur is benign if the client denies chest pain
options.C: Wait until the next scheduled shift assessment before reporting it
options.D: Record only the heart rate because extra heart sounds are outside the nursing assessment

candidate.rationale: NCBI Nursing Skills identifies murmurs as extra heart sounds and instructs nurses to communicate new murmurs that were not previously documented to the health care provider. The finding should also be documented as part of the cardiovascular assessment. Absence of chest pain does not make a new murmur automatically benign, delayed reporting is inappropriate, and assessment of extra heart sounds is part of nursing cardiovascular assessment.
candidate.source_claim_supported: A newly detected murmur not previously documented is an abnormal cardiovascular assessment finding that should be documented and reported to the health care provider.
candidate.source_locator: Auscultation > Extra Heart Sounds: murmurs are blowing/whooshing sounds associated with turbulent blood flow; new murmurs not previously recorded should be immediately communicated to the health care provider; Table 9.3d lists new extra heart sounds as unexpected findings to document and notify
candidate.source_organization: National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI) — Open RN Nursing Skills
candidate.source_version_date: Nursing Skills 2nd edition, 2023; current NCBI page accessed 2026-08-17
candidate.stem: During a focused cardiovascular assessment, the nurse auscultates the standard cardiac areas and hears a murmur that is not documented in the client's record. What is the most appropriate nursing action?
